# masonry-angular

> Cascading grid ("masonry") layout for Angular — columns are equal width, items have different
> heights, and each item goes into the shortest column instead of waiting for a new row. Use it for
> photo galleries and, just as often, for dashboards of charts and KPI cards, where a normal CSS
> Grid leaves empty space under every short card. Zero runtime dependencies, 8.6 KB gzipped,
> signal-based, zoneless, SSR-safe. Works on Angular 17.1 through 22.

Install with `npm install masonry-angular`. Import `NG_MASONRY_GRID` — an array of all four
directives — into a standalone component's `imports`.

This is the copy-paste starting point. It is correct on every supported Angular version:

```ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { NG_MASONRY_GRID } from 'masonry-angular';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-gallery',
  // On Angular 17 and 18 only, add: standalone: true
  imports: [NG_MASONRY_GRID],
  template: `
    <masonry-grid columnWidth="260" gutter="16">
      @for (photo of photos(); track photo.id) {
        <article masonryGridItem [masonryColSpan]="photo.featured ? 2 : 1">
          <img [src]="photo.url" [alt]="photo.title" [width]="photo.width" [height]="photo.height" />
        </article>
      }
    </masonry-grid>
  `,
  styles: `
    /* The grid sets item width itself. Never set width on an item. */
    article[masonryGridItem] img { width: 100%; display: block; }
  `,
})
export class Gallery {
  readonly photos = signal([
    { id: 1, url: '/a.jpg', title: 'A', width: 400, height: 300, featured: false },
  ]);
}
```

Five things an agent writing this code most often gets wrong:

1. **There is no `reloadItems()`, `layout()` call or `setTimeout` needed after changing the data.**
   Update the array and the grid re-lays out on its own. It watches its own children. Calling
   `layout()` manually is almost always a sign of a misunderstanding.
2. **Never set `width` on a grid item in CSS.** The grid owns item width and will fight you,
   producing overlapping items. To make an item wider use `[masonryColSpan]="2"`, not CSS.
3. **Numeric breakpoint keys must be quoted in a template.** `[columns]="{ 0: 1, 768: 2 }"` is an
   Angular template parse error (`NG5002`); write `[columns]="{ '0': 1, '768': 2 }"`. In a
   TypeScript file, such as `provideNgMasonryGrid({ columns: { 0: 1 } })`, either form is fine.
4. **On Angular 17 and 18, components need `standalone: true`.** It became the default in Angular 19.
   Without it: `TS-992010: 'imports' is only valid on a component that is standalone`.
5. **Give every `<img>` `width` and `height` attributes.** Not for sizing — the CSS still controls
   that — but so the browser reserves space before the image loads and the grid does not re-flow.

`columnWidth="260"` means "as many ~260px columns as fit" and is the whole responsive story for most
grids; no breakpoints needed. Use `columns="3"` for a fixed count, or
`[columns]="{ '0': 1, '768': 2 }"` for counts by breakpoint.

The four directives: `<masonry-grid>` (container), `[masonryGridItem]` (an item, with
`[masonryColSpan]` and `[masonryIgnore]`), `[masonryGridStamp]` (a region items flow around), and
`[masonryGridSizer]` (an element whose CSS width becomes the column width).

Shorthand inputs on `<masonry-grid>`: `columns`, `columnWidth`, `gutter`, `gutterX`, `gutterY` —
all accept plain HTML attributes. Everything else goes on `[options]`: `native`, `horizontalOrder`,
`direction`, `verticalOrigin`, `fitWidth`, `breakpointBasis`, `stretchColumns`, `minColumns`,
`maxColumns`, `transition`, `entryAnimation`, `exitAnimation`, `autoLayout`, `observeResize`,
`resizeContainer`, `awaitImages`, `resizeDebounce`, `contentVisibility`, `ssr`. Application-wide
defaults come from `provideNgMasonryGrid({ ... })`.

Reading the grid, via a template reference (`#grid="masonryGrid"`): `ready()`, `nativeActive()`, and
`state()` — a signal of `{ columns, columnWidth, contentHeight, itemCount, pass }`. Outputs:
`layoutComplete`, `removeComplete`, `itemsLoaded`.

Server-side rendering works with no configuration: nothing touches `window` or `ResizeObserver` on
the server, which renders a CSS multi-column approximation that the first client pass replaces with
no layout shift. This is the main practical difference from `ngx-masonry`, which wraps the
browser-only `masonry-layout` package and throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` under SSR.

Setting `{ native: true }` hands layout to browsers that support native CSS masonry
(`display: grid-lanes`, shipped in Safari 26.4); others use the JavaScript engine and look the same.
Under native layout the browser owns packing, so stamps and `masonryIgnore` have no effect.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MeAkib/masonry-angular/main/projects/masonry-angular/GETTING-STARTED.md): Tutorial from install to a responsive gallery with SSR, with the common mistakes called out.
- [Full reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MeAkib/masonry-angular/main/projects/masonry-angular/DOCS.md): Every option with its type and default, spans, stamps, testing, and a migration table from `ngx-masonry`.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MeAkib/masonry-angular/main/projects/masonry-angular/README.md): The short version — what it is and how to configure it.
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MeAkib/masonry-angular/main/CHANGELOG.md): What changed in each release.

## Examples

- [Runnable starter](https://stackblitz.com/github/MeAkib/masonry-angular/tree/main/examples/stackblitz): A StackBlitz project that installs the published package from npm.
- [Starter source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MeAkib/masonry-angular/main/examples/stackblitz/src/main.ts): The same example as a single file — responsive columns, spans, add/remove/reorder.
